title: Development Compass — Q1/Q2 2026 (personal notes)
content:
Context: role = Senior People Ops Partner (L&D + org design focus). These are working thoughts for upcoming manager 1:1 and my mid-year reflection. Informal — raw bullets, questions, TODOs.

Purpose: quick snapshot of wins, stretch areas, asks for manager, and a 6–12 month development path that I can refine with feedback.

Key wins (evidence / quick data):
- Designed and launched micro-learning pilot for infra eng team (12 sessions, 78% active participation). Post-survey net promotor ~+22 vs baseline.
- Ran two manager training cohorts; median peer rating for facilitation = 4.5/5. Saved ~120 hours of 1:1 coaching time across org (est).
- Led org-design review for Dedicated product team; identified 3 role duplications and proposed simplified scope map — accepted and scheduled for next sprint.
- Reduced time-to-hire for senior IC roles from 56 -> 41 days (process tweaks + hiring panel checklist).

Concrete metrics I own / want to surface:
- L&D active participation rate (goal 60% company-wide) — current 43% (infra pilot bumped team to 78%).
- Manager enablement completion rate — cohort 1 = 92% completion, cohort 2 running.
- Hiring funnel time to offer median.
- Peer feedback score (internal): aim for >=4.4; current snapshot 4.2.

Development goals (6–12 months):
1) Strategic influence: push from program delivery to strategic partner for product orgs.
   - Outcome: be invited to roadmap planning for at least 2 product teams by Q3.
   - Signals: run two org health reviews that lead to prioritized headcount/ownership changes.
2) Coaching + upward influence: level up ability to coach managers on stakeholder prioritization and tradeoffs.
   - Outcome: managers report improved clarity on tradeoffs in post-coaching surveys (target +15 pts).
3) Cross-functional visibility: present L&D impact story to GTM and Eng leadership (exec forum).
4) Promotion readiness: document examples that map to criteria for Senior Manager (org-level impact, cross-functional influence).

Evidence / examples to collect for promotion packet: (short notes)
- Case study: infra micro-learning pilot — objective, design choices, results, business impact (hiring speed, onboarding time).
- Case study: manager training program (curriculum, cohort outcomes, recorded feedback).
- Org design recommendation for Dedicated team (before/after org chart + rationale + outcome).
- Stakeholder testimonials: ask Jonah and Priya for 1–2 lines each about impact.

Manager prep / asks for next 1:1:
- Calibration ask: honest read on promotion trajectory — what’s blocking me? Specific behaviors to demonstrate.
- Resource ask: 0.2 FTE PM time for Q2 to productize two popular workshops into a repeatable product. Rationale + estimated ROI.
- Sponsor ask: would you introduce me in the Product Leadership sync next month? I’ll present 12-min impact story.
- Feedback request: where have I been over-indexing (tactically) vs under-indexing (strategically)? Examples?
- Career conversation: interest in people-lead vs principal IC path. Need clarity on how to choose + what metrics to hit for each.

Stretch projects I’d like (ranked):
- 1) Lead a cross-org onboarding rework with infra + SRE — measurable metric: new hire time-to-first-commit.
- 2) Partner with Product on feature adoption playbook (L4 owners) — build post-launch enablement.
- 3) Small leadership rotation: 3 months embedded with Console PMs to build product empathy.

Blockers / risks:
- Time: running two cohorts + pilot content creation is bleeding execution time; need at least 0.2 FTE support.
- Measurement: lack of consistent company-wide L&D baseline metric (I need analytics help from Observability team).
- Stakeholder bandwidth: Product leadership calendar is heavily booked; need manager to broker intro.

Short term action items (next 30 days):
- Draft promotion evidence doc (outline + one completed case study) — due: 2026-03-31.
- Ask Jonah for 2-line testimonial and permission to include his quote — due: 2026-03-20.
- Prepare 12-min 'L&D impact' deck for Product Leadership (ask manager for intro) — due: 2026-04-10.
- Create measurement ask: quick note for Observability owners to request cohort analytics support.

Questions I want to surface to skip-level / manager:
- When you think of people ops leaders who scale beyond tactical ops, what patterns stand out? (Specific behaviors/examples please.)
- Is the company more likely to reward a people-lead that can drive measurable product outcomes or one that builds deep org capabilities? Which signals should I prioritize?

Loose ideas / experiments (brainstorm):
- Office hours for product teams: 30-min weekly drop-in focused on onboarding + adoption. Experiment x6 weeks with Dedicated PMs.
- Micro-mentorship pairs across eng and product for 1:1 shadowing.
- Convert top 3 workshop modules into short asynchronous videos + worksheets — reduces facilitation lift.

Notes to self (voice memos / reminders):
- Keep evidence concise: numbers + 1 direct quote per case study.
- When asking for promotion, align examples to rubric language (ownership, measurable impact, scaling ability).
- Practice 2-minute pitch for each case study.

TODO quick list (tick boxes mentally):
- [ ] Draft promotion outline
- [ ] Collect Jonah + Priya quotes
- [ ] Request 0.2 FTE approval template from manager
- [ ] Schedule dry run of Product Leadership deck

Emotional check-in (meta):
- Feeling energized by impact but stretched. Need explicit permission to offload tactical work.
- Goal: keep curiosity high, protect deep work blocks twice/week.

End notes: save this as living doc. Will iterate post-1:1 and after collecting first case study metrics.

-- Ava M.
